explainBack.question: Why would drawing a rough sketch and placing a comment on one area produce a better result than writing a single longer, more detailed prompt?
explainBack.answer: Because words describe spatial layout ambiguously while a sketch supplies the arrangement directly—the system receives a rough map of where the sofa, headline space or product should sit. A comment then bounds the edit to a small target (this sleeve, that lamp), so the regeneration is constrained to the intended region instead of the model reinterpreting the whole scene from a long verbal description. The limit still holds: the output is a newly generated image, not an editable file, so exact text and measurements need checking outside the picture.
